header: Date: 2025-10-29 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: enabled | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood Product), Ellen Brooks (Lyra ML), Samir Khatri (Lyra Platform), Priya Menon (Lyra Security)
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo focused on multi-tenant controls: org vs project API keys, quota enforcement, burst capacity, and console flows to manage tenants. Customer cares about strict tenant isolation, predictable per-team quotas, audit logs, and a short PoC to validate throughput. Action items: pricing sheet, benchmark script, SOC2/network docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Ellen Brooks: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Maya.
[00:07] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: show console flows for org and project key creation, demo API calls for rate limits and quotas, then talk about Optimize suggestions for batching and caching, and leave time for security questions.
[00:18] Samir Khatri: That sounds good. Our goals — we need per-team hard quotas, ability to throttle noisy users, and strong audit logs.
[00:25] Jonas Reed: Perfect. We'll start in the Console. One note, sorry if the screen shares a little slow — using my VPN.
[00:30] [screen share starts]
[00:33] Jonas: Here is the top-level org page. You can see an Org-level quota that caps token usage across all child projects.
[00:40] Priya (interrupting): Is that enforced at the gateway, or do you rely on eventual counters?
[00:45] Jonas: Great question. Enforcement is at the routing gateway — we maintain counters with soft and hard thresholds. Soft thresholds will emit warnings and metrics, hard thresholds reject with 429 and include the quota metadata in the response. Occasionally the transcription on our internal docs shows, uh, "h-29" but it's 429, sorry.
[00:58] Ellen: And for per-team isolation — how do we do sticky routing so that a project stays on the same dedicated pool?
[01:04] Jonas: You can pin a project key to a Dedicated pool or to a region. We have sticky routing policies: session affinity for longer conversations, and when capacity is constrained the routing policy falls back to compatible variants.
[01:13] Samir: Do you support burst capacity if a product releases an anniversary campaign? We need temporary burst without changing long-term quotas.
[01:18] Lina Gomez: Yes — burst windows can be configured at the project level. You set burst quota minutes and a cap on concurrency; the platform enforces fairshare so other teams don't get starved.
[01:25] Ellen: Happy path looks good. What about token accounting — do we count input + output?
[01:29] Jonas: We count tokens both directions; you can opt for a compact accounting mode that charges only output tokens for internal workloads, though that is only recommended for trusted internal projects because it affects reproducibility and cost attribution.
[01:40] [01:40] Samir: Can we create API keys programmatically? We don't want to click in the console for each microservice.
[01:44] Maya: Absolutely; there's an Org API to create project keys and attach quota profiles. I'll paste the sample curl in the Slack thread after the call.
[01:51] Jonas: Example: POST /v1/orgs/:org_id/projects with body {"name":"analytics-pipeline","quota_profile":"team-medium"} which returns a project key and default limits.
[02:00] Priya: For compliance, we need audit logs that show key creation, token usage spikes, and admin actions. Does the console expose those?
[02:06] Jonas: Yes — Audit Logs tab provides immutable events with actor, timestamp, and before/after. Logs can stream to your SIEM via syslog or to an S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS.
[02:15] Priya: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:18] Maya: Yes, we support external KMS and HSM for private deployments. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS but can shift to customer KMS for Private deployments.
[02:28] Ellen: What about SSO and RBAC? We need Okta and role-based granular permissions so only certain ops folks can change quotas.
[02:34] Jonas: SAML/Okta works; RBAC has built-in roles and custom roles. You can grant quota-management only to a small admin group and restrict project creation elsewhere.
[02:42] [02:42] Samir: Can we set concurrency limits per key and also global concurrency?
[02:47] Lina: Yes. Concurrency operates as a separate dimension from token quotas. You can configure per-key concurrency and org-level headroom. If a project reaches concurrency limit calls are queued briefly and then denied.
[02:56] Ellen: Demo the API behavior when a project hits soft threshold.
[03:00] Jonas: Sure. I'll run a script that emits 150 concurrent requests to the same project. You may hear some pauses.
[03:05] [03:05] Jonas: Running... you can see metrics emitting in the Console: token rate, rps, active connections. Soft threshold triggers a warning event and we start returning 429 with X-Redwood-Quota-Warning header.
[03:17] Samir: Will that header help the client backoff algorithm?
[03:20] Jonas: Exactly, it includes recommended retry-after and current window consumption. For SDKs we provide an exponential backoff helper that reads those headers.
[03:27] Priya: Are there tenant-level network isolation options for Private deployments? We need VPC peering or on-prem connectivity.
[03:33] Maya: For Private we support VPC-nested deployments and air-gapped installs. Our network diagram (I'll send) shows optional peering or direct connect and per-tenant routing tables.
[03:41] Ellen: On the Optimize side, you mentioned caching. How does prefix caching interact with multi-tenant quotas?
[03:48] Lina: Prefix/KV caching reduces token usage by serving repeated prefixes from cache; cache hits still count toward a separate cache operation quota, which you can limit per project, so heavy cache use doesn't blow past org budgets. Also cache is namespace-scoped so projects can't read each other's cached entries.
[04:01] [04:01] Samir: What about billing granularity — can we bill back to teams by project key?
[04:05] Maya: Yes, we generate token-level cost breakdowns by project key and route them into billing exports. You can map project keys to cost centers.
[04:12] Ellen: Let's talk attack scenarios — what if a leaked key starts spamming large-generation requests to exhaust org quota?
[04:19] Jonas: You can set per-key daily caps, automatic key rotation policies, and sudden-spike detection rules that quarantine keys and send alerts. We also support rate-limiting by token and by RPS simultaneously.
[04:30] Priya: Do you have a demo for the quarantine flow?
[04:33] Jonas: Quick simulated demo: I'm toggling a rule that quarantines keys once they exceed 500k tokens in an hour. The console flags the key and marks it quarantined; calls return 403 with a quarantine code and we create an incident in the audit logs.
[04:46] [04:46] Ellen: Nice. One concern: how deterministic is routing for latency-sensitive flows? We need <50ms P50 for single-turn responses.
[04:52] Lina: For latency SLOs we recommend dedicated pools with pinned models and smaller batch sizes, and you can enable low-latency mode. We showed a P50 of ~28ms on our benchmark for similar-sized models on dedicated hardware; we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:06] Samir: For the PoC we want to validate end-to-end throughput and latency for our conversational embeddings workload. What's the recommended starter configuration?
[05:12] Maya: Recommend a Dedicated 2-GPU pool for your baseline, project keys pinned to that pool, and a moderate token quota plus burst windows. We'll run a 5-day pilot with traffic replay.
[05:21] Ellen: How intrusive is traffic replay — will we need to ship payloads?
[05:24] Jonas: We'll take sanitized logs or a sample set. Our SEs can help build a replay harness that respects PII rules.
[05:31] Priya: Last security question — does Redwood keep generated outputs for any hosted customers? We need assurances on retention and deletion.
[05:37] Maya: By default we retain short metrics for performance but not customer data for hosted enterprise accounts; retention policies can be set per-org, and Private customers control retention entirely. We'll share the data retention policy document.
[05:48] [05:48] Ellen: Great. Let's wrap with the ask and next steps.
[05:52] Maya: Recap: We'll send pricing sheet and a demo benchmark script; schedule a 1-week PoC to run the throughput test; Redwood to share SOC2/network/KMS docs.
[06:01] Samir: Sounds good. Thanks for the demo, Jonas and Lina.
[06:04] Maya: Thanks all. I'll follow up in email and Slack.
[06:08] [call ends]
